title: Procuring or offering a false or forged instrument for public filing
summary: Knowingly procuring or offering a false or forged instrument for filing, registration or recording in a California public office when a genuine instrument of that kind could lawfully be filed. The offering itself can complete the offense; actual recording or successful fraud is not required. Each instrument and statutory procurement/offer is separately punishable.
penalty: Felony: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison under section 18(a). A discretionary base fine up to $10,000 may apply under section 672. Section 115(c) limits probation for specified repeat or multiple-violation cases, subject to its unusual-case exception. Adult individual base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Knowledge that the qualifying instrument is false or forged.

title: Injuring, destroying, concealing or disposing of insured property to defraud the insurer
summary: Willfully injuring, destroying, secreting, abandoning or disposing of property insured against theft, embezzlement or casualty, intending to defraud or prejudice the insurer. The property may belong to anyone. Fire is expressly excluded from casualty for this section; fire-related insurance fraud requires a different analysis.
penalty: Felony: 2, 3 or 5 years under section 1170(h), plus a base fine up to $50,000. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily county jail subject to state-prison exclusions. Section 548(b) adds two years for each qualifying prior conviction if alleged and admitted or proved. Adult individual base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Willful conduct with intent to defraud or prejudice the insurer.

title: Making a false written financial statement to obtain a benefit
summary: Knowingly making or causing a false written statement about financial condition or ability to pay, intending reliance to procure one of the property, cash, loan, credit, guaranty or commercial-paper benefits specified in (1), for yourself or a represented or interested person or business. Actual receipt of the benefit is not required for this making-statement route.
penalty: Misdemeanor: up to six months in county jail, a base fine up to $1,000, or both under section 532a(4). The distinct false-identity branch in (4) has different penalties. Adult individual base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review.
mentalState: Knowledge of falsity and intent that the statement be relied on for the specified benefit.

title: Obtaining a benefit through a false written financial statement

penalty: Misdemeanor: up to six months in county jail, a base fine up to $1,000, or both under section 532a(4). The distinct false-identity branch in (4) has different penalties. title: False financial statement using fictitious or impersonated identity
summary: Committing an offense under section 532a(1), (2) or (3) using a fictitious name, social security number, business name or address, or falsely presenting yourself as another person or business. This entry is the aggravated false-identity sentence of (4), not the ordinary misdemeanor penalty sentence.
penalty: Felony or misdemeanor: 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h), a base fine up to $5,000, or both; alternatively up to one year in county jail, a base fine up to $2,500, or both. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily county jail subject to state-prison exclusions. Adult individual base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review. Any stated one-year misdemeanor term is capped at 364 days under Penal Code section 18.5.

title: Misappropriation of public money: unauthorized appropriation

Incidental and minimal use authorized by Government Code section 8314 is excluded. Knowledge of the lack of legal authority or the legal duty, or criminal negligence in failing to ascertain it; ordinary carelessness alone is insufficient.
penalty: Felony: 2, 3 or 4 years in state prison and disqualification from holding any office in California. A discretionary base fine up to $10,000 may apply under section 672. title: Repeated failure to file, or false tax filings or information
summary: For covered California income/franchise taxes, repeatedly failing to file required returns or supply information, or repeatedly making or supplying knowingly false or fraudulent filings or information, over at least two years and resulting in estimated delinquent tax liability of at least $15,000. CALCRIM 2800 and 2810 retain the repetition requirement for both routes; intent to evade is not required. Corporate-officer and filing presumptions are not conclusive proof. The criminal punishment sentence excludes people who are mentally incompetent or have dementia, Alzheimer's disease or a similar condition.
penalty: Misdemeanor: up to one year of imprisonment, a base fine up to $5,000, or both, plus investigation and prosecution costs. Section 19701 also describes a separately recoverable penalty up to $5,000; the criminal fine is not a total liability cap. Adult individual base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review. Any stated one-year misdemeanor term is capped at 364 days under Penal Code section 18.5.
mentalState: Intent to evade is not required. The false-filing/information route requires knowledge of falsity under CALCRIM 2810; the duty, repeated conduct and delinquency threshold must be proved.

Willfulness means intentional violation of a known legal duty, not simply an unpaid balance. The criminal punishment sentence excludes people who are mentally incompetent or have dementia, Alzheimer's disease or a similar condition.
penalty: Misdemeanor: up to one year of imprisonment, a base fine up to $5,000, or both, plus investigation and prosecution costs. title: Willful nonfiling or false tax information with intent to evade
summary: Willfully failing to file a required return or supply information on time, or willfully making false or fraudulent returns, statements or information, with intent to evade covered California income or corporation taxes. A good-faith misunderstanding of the legal duty must not be treated as intentional evasion.
penalty: Felony or misdemeanor: up to one year in county jail or 16 months, 2 years or 3 years in state prison under Penal Code section 18(a), a base fine up to $20,000, or both fine and imprisonment, plus investigation and prosecution costs. The statute specifies state prison, not section 1170(h). Adult individual base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review. Any stated one-year misdemeanor term is capped at 364 days under Penal Code section 18.5.

title: Signing a materially false tax document under penalty of perjury
summary: Willfully making and signing a tax return, statement or document under penalty of perjury without believing it true and correct in every material matter. A material falsehood and intentional violation of a known duty must be proved; proof of additional tax owed is not required. A signature alone is not conclusive proof of who signed.
penalty: Felony, with misdemeanor treatment available under Penal Code sections 17(b) and 18(b): 16 months, 2 years or 3 years under section 1170(h), or up to one year in county jail under section 18(b), or the stated fine, or both as permitted. Section 1170(h) custody is ordinarily county jail subject to state-prison exclusions. The individual base fine is up to $50,000; for a corporation the statutory ceiling is $200,000. Investigation and prosecution costs are additional. Adult individual base penalties are shown. Restitution, assessments, enhancements, probation and case-specific sentencing require separate review. Any stated one-year misdemeanor term is capped at 364 days under Penal Code section 18.5.
mentalState: Voluntary, intentional violation of a known legal duty and lack of belief in material accuracy.
